objective: Al terminar debates problemas sociales (pobreza, vivienda, desempleo, discriminación) con vocabulario preciso, causas, consecuencias y posibles soluciones.

warmup.prompt_es: Hablar de problemas sociales exige vocabulario matizado y tacto. Practicas describir causas, consecuencias y soluciones, y expresar tu postura sin generalizar.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Today we're discussing homelessness. Dr. Silva, why has it become such a visible problem in our cities?
lines.es: Hoy hablamos del sinhogarismo. Dra. Silva, ¿por qué se ha convertido en un problema tan visible en nuestras ciudades?

lines.speaker: Dr. Silva
lines.text: There isn't a single cause. Rising rents, job insecurity, cuts to mental health services and family breakdown all play a part. For many people, one unexpected event, such as a job loss or an illness, is enough to push them into crisis.
lines.es: No hay una única causa. El aumento de los alquileres, la inestabilidad laboral, los recortes en salud mental y la ruptura familiar influyen. Para muchas personas, un acontecimiento inesperado, como perder el trabajo o una enfermedad, basta para empujarlas a la crisis.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Some people say homeless individuals are responsible for their own situation.
lines.es: Algunos dicen que las personas sin hogar son responsables de su situación.

lines.speaker: Dr. Silva
lines.text: That's an oversimplification. The evidence shows that most people end up on the streets because of circumstances beyond their control. Blaming individuals doesn't solve anything.
lines.es: Es una simplificación excesiva. Las pruebas muestran que la mayoría acaba en la calle por circunstancias fuera de su control. Culpar a las personas no resuelve nada.

lines.speaker: Dr. Silva
lines.text: Housing First programmes have been very successful. They provide stable housing first, and then offer support with health, addiction and employment. Countries that have adopted them have seen a significant reduction in rough sleeping.
lines.es: Los programas 'Housing First' han tenido mucho éxito. Ofrecen primero vivienda estable y después apoyo en salud, adicciones y empleo. Los países que los han adoptado han visto una reducción significativa de personas durmiendo en la calle.

lines.speaker: Dr. Silva
lines.text: In the short term, yes. But in the long run, it costs less than emergency services, hospital admissions and prison. Prevention is always cheaper than cure.
lines.es: A corto plazo, sí. Pero a largo plazo cuesta menos que servicios de emergencia, ingresos hospitalarios y prisión. Prevenir siempre es más barato que curar.

glossary.example: It pays off in the long run.

md_es: **Vocabulario de problemas sociales**
| Tema | Palabras clave |
| Pobreza | *poverty line, deprivation, cost of living, food bank, welfare, benefits, inequality* |
| Vivienda | *homelessness, affordable housing, eviction, rent, landlord, overcrowding* |
| Trabajo | *unemployment, job insecurity, zero-hours contract, gig economy, living wage* |
| Discriminación | *prejudice, stereotype, racism, sexism, ageism, equal opportunities, diversity* |
| Salud y bienestar | *mental health, addiction, loneliness, access to healthcare* |
| Comunidad | *social cohesion, integration, volunteering, community, solidarity* |
**Hablar de causas y consecuencias**
- Causas: *X is caused by Y · X results from Y · X is due to Y · X stems from Y · X is a consequence of Y.*
- Consecuencias: *X leads to Y · X results in Y · X gives rise to Y · As a result, … · Consequently, …*
**Hablar de soluciones**
- *One possible solution is … · It could be argued that … · The government should … · What is needed is …*
- *Prevention is better than cure. · A holistic approach is required.*
**Evitar los estereotipos**
- Usa *some / many / a growing number of / in many cases* en lugar de *all / always / never*.
- *People experiencing homelessness* (más respetuoso) en lugar de *the homeless*.
- Distingue hechos de opiniones: *Studies show … · It is widely believed that …*
**Expresar tu postura con tacto**
- *I would argue that … · It seems to me that … · I'm inclined to think … · To some extent, … but …*
**Errores típicos**
- ✘ *The homeless are lazy.* → ✔ *There is no evidence that homelessness is caused by laziness.*
- ✘ *The poverty are increasing.* → ✔ *Poverty is increasing.*
- ✘ *It's the fault of the government that … (generalización)* → ✔ *Government policy has contributed to …*
- ✘ *A lot of people has lost their jobs.* → ✔ *A lot of people have lost their jobs.*
- ✘ *It depends of the circumstances.* → ✔ *It depends on the circumstances.*
**Ojo:** *poor* (adjetivo) ≠ *the poor* (los pobres, colectivo plural); *poverty* (sustantivo). *Fewer* con contables, *less* con incontables. *Benefits* (UK) = ayudas sociales; *welfare* (US).
Pronunciación: *homelessness* /ˈhəʊmləsnəs/ · *eviction* /ɪˈvɪkʃn/ · *prejudice* /ˈpredʒədɪs/ · *stem from* /stem frɒm/.
